object_description: four staggered prismatic volumes around a central courtyard
design_condition: The volumes are arranged around a central courtyard and placed toward one side of the site to preserve mature trees, create a park-like perimeter, and connect the campus naturally to the surrounding district.

positive.statement: The carefully proportioned courtyard figure integrates the denser campus well into the garden-city context.
The arrangement preserves many large-crowned trees and creates varied, connected outdoor spaces.
Giving each school level its own building strengthens address and makes orientation easier.
The school wings provide a solid and flexible spatial structure for contemporary teaching and learning.
The schoolyard and community centre offer welcome public added value and a point of identification.
Good space efficiency, compactness, timber construction and large photovoltaic areas promise a favourable cost and CO2 balance.

negative.statement: The enclosure of the anterooms may fragment the open space and reduce its generosity.
The proximity of the volumes to the neighbouring path reduces the quality of the vegetative border.
A direct line of sight to the community-centre entrance from the street is desirable.
The community centre’s mix of uses does not yet provide sufficient operational synergies.
The SKB access organization does not match the qualities of the other school wings.
The school’s architectural expression remains schematic and uniform, giving it a somewhat temporary feel.
The revised north-facing catering rooms may have seriously limited quality of stay because of insufficient sunlight.
The roof structure makes the community building appear less open than previously indicated.
The large footprint creates cramped ground-level open spaces, particularly around the running track.
The urban-planning approach severely impairs the surrounding green space and reduces its generosity and depth.
